title: Maize lethal necrosis disease in maize - Zambia

Header: Maize lethal necrosis disease in maize - Zambia
Maize lethal necrosis disease (MLN) ( combination of two viruses , Maize Chlorotic Mottle Virus ( MCMoV ) and Sugarcane Mosaic Virus ( SCMV ) or other cereal viruses )

Prevention: Plant certified seed from reliable suppliers; report anyone importing seed unofficially.
Rotate maize with non-cereal crops, such as sweet potato, beans, garlic, onion, for a period of 2-3 seasons if
MLN had attacked your or neighbouring fields.
Do not plant maize near fields with infested maize (less than 500m) as the disease will spread into your field.
Avoid movement of green maize from infected to disease- free areas.
Eliminate host plants (weeds) of thrips, aphids & plant hoppers and clear/ burn grass around the field.
Plant with fertilizer and manure to enhance crop nutrition and vigour.

MLND causes yellow stripes that later lead to drying, stunted growth, failure to tassel, no grain filling in cobs and death of the whole plant leading to the whole field having plants with dried appearance
Angular leaf spot disease also causes necrotic dead leaf areas but only in spots and not entire leaf edges or leaves as for
MLN Consider taking action as soon as few plants shows these symptoms
Look for thrips (tiny yellowish-green slender insects) and leafhoppers (small 0.5 cm greenish insects, jumping) on leaves as they spread the disease.
If planthoppers and thrips are seen on a number of plants you may consider action if disease is in neighbouring fields or has just arrived in your field.

Plants that are infected late in development remain unproductive, and are barren or bear small, partially filled, malformed ears.
